utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, good morning. Madam Registrar, could you call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, ma'am. All the accused are here. Same goes for the Defence teams. Everyone seems to be present. Prosecution is Mr. Thayer and Mr. Nicholls that I can see. Let's go into private session for a short while, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is a motion from the Prosecution for authorisation to reply, which we will be considering. We will be handing down an oral decision early next week. But it will be an oral decision, not a written one. I just wanted to alert you to that. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Good morning Your Honour, and counsel. I just wanted to say that Mr. McCloskey apologises for not being able to be here this morning. He will be coming in later. He had some work to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay, thank you. It's good to hear that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning to you, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I welcome you on behalf of my colleagues and myself. We are going to proceed with your testimony. We will try to finish today, but I don't promise you that. Mr. Bourgon, you were in possession of the floor when we adjourned yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My first question this morning, Witness, is very simple. I would just like to know the date on which you were relocated?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 10th of October.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of which year?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, we have information, Witness, concerning the fact that you are a regular -- person who regularly watches the proceedings of this Tribunal from your house (redacted). Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, any ordinary citizen of the former Yugoslavia would be curious. They are all following the proceedings. B92 for instance regularly broadcast all the proceedings, and any normal person would show an interest in that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My question, Witness, is quite straightforward. And I take it that you consider yourself as a normal person and that you have been watching proceedings from this Tribunal. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only do I consider myself normal, there are all others who consider me normal.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My next question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a television set, and of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And if I can just ask you to, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, how many hours a day are you listening to these proceedings or have you listened to the proceedings of this Tribunal on TV?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Whenever I had time to spare and did not have any work obligations, because you ought to know that I am an active person still, I listen to the proceedings. But I do not set aside time specifically for that. In other words, whenever I had time, I review reports or I just watch short clips at any time during the day that I'm free.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Before going on to my next question, I would just like to make a correction in yesterday's transcript. I spoke with my colleague already about this correction. It appears that it was made, but in the -- I do not have the updated version and would I like the witness to confirm this correction. Witness, I will read you a quote of what you said yesterday and simply ask you for a correction. Yesterday, that was on page 15, lines 20 to 25, you said the following: "I only knew Drago, or Dragan, Nikolic. I believe his name is Dragan Nikolic. I knew him because he spent a great deal of time in the barracks, and I would come across him just as anyone else. I knew him personally as a decent person, a pedantic person. He was rated as an officer," and this is where we get to the part I would like to correct, because in yesterday's transcript it says, "As an officer who was arrogant or taxing on anyone." I would simply like you to confirm that what the transcript should read, in accordance with your answer from yesterday, is that, "He was rated as an officer who was not arrogant, nor taxing on anyone." Can you confirm this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You need to say "ne" or "da". I couldn't hear. I was watching him. Oh, I see.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. The microphones were not on. Precisely. As you put it; a fine man. And this wasn't just my opinion, but the opinion of all the others in the barracks. He was a communicative person, an affable person who did not try to be to be effusive in showing that he is an officer. You know what I'm trying to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, I can confirm it is so updated.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I will move on to my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I thank you, Judge Kwon. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I will move on to my next question which relates to this one. On the basis of your statement, which you provided to the Prosecution in November of 2005, I would like you to confirm that in July of 1995 you did not know the name Drago Nikolic. The name. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there was confusion during interpretation or a play of words. I said that I wasn't sure whether he was Drago or Dragan, and this might have been interpreted as if I didn't, in fact, know the man. But I cannot claim not to have known him since I've spent a certain period of time together with him in the barracks. This might have been an error in interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I will quote you from your statement of November 2005, and that is at paragraph 5. And if need be, I can show it to you on the screen where you say in this statement, "At the time, he was the senior security officer of the Zvornik Brigade, but I did not know his name." Which is true today, that you might have remembered or that you did not know his name? Is it the statement or what you are saying today that is the truth?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: It wouldn't be normal for me not to know the man. As I said, it may have been due to interpretation that it came across this way, because I only said that I wasn't sure whether his name was Dragan or Drago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll leave it at that because I will ask anyway for the -- your statement to be on the record for the sake of confirming whether what you are saying today is the right version. I move to my next question. You said yesterday, and this is on the -- at page 49 of the transcript at lines 1 to 16, and I will not quote but say basically the substance. You confirmed that you asked and were granted a two to three days leave after the Orahovac events in order to leave Zvornik and take some rest. Can you confirm that this morning?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I asked that we go somewhere where there are no uniformed persons, no soldiers, in order to find some psychological rest, but then the chief -- there, again, I wanted to refer to Pantic, him or the person substituting for him, namely Miso, proved to be quite obliging, which was something of a rarity at the time in the barracks, because I was allowed to spend nights at home with my wife and children. I wasn't compelled to sleep in the barracks which was the norm at the time. So he was lenient in that respect. He allowed me to spend the night in the barracks and then the following morning I was supposed to report to the barracks before the actual waking time, and at that point I was granted a few days' leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That's the -- the last part of your question [sic] is actually what I was looking for. And please try to answer the question that I ask, just so that we can move along more quickly. Again, I never want to interrupt you, but it goes better if you try to answer the question that was asked.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: May I have 3D80 on the e-court, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is this the attendance sheet?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No, that's the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, it is being brought to my attention that maybe the English translation of your last answer is not exactly what you said. Now, if you look -- well, you cannot read English, so I would -- it says here in the transcript, "And at that point I was granted a few days' leave." Now, what I'm looking for is whether you were -- you asked for three days' leave after the Orahovac events and were granted those days. Is that the situation?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, in the aftermath of every difficult situation at the front-line, I always asked for a few days off a to pull myself together, and that was the case again this time. However, further developments proved to be so grievous and dark that I was one of the rare cases who could be granted something like that because this person was a neighbour of mine. And he allowed me to spend the nights at home to spend time with my sons, and this allowed me to rest psychologically. So this is what they did. This is how obliging they were.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry to interrupt. I was told that in the answer which is being corrected now that there is another error. What the witness said was that -- not at that point I was granted a few days' leave, but that I was granted leave that would take place at a point when it was possible or when I could take leave. So what he said was he was granted in principle that he could take leave but not at that point, is what I've been told.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. You have -- Witness. Witness. Has this been, this conversation, this exchange, has it been translated to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, I can't -- I can't claim to be an expert in -- in Serbo-Croat language, but I understand enough to know that "ne" means no, and "da" means yes. What I want to know -- Witness, look at me, please. Mr. Nicholls has just made a statement. Was that statement translated to you in your own language?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean here?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes. A minute ago.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters apologise: We heard him say yes. Could the witness come closer to the microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but this "yes" now --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you come closer to the microphones, please. Mr. Nicholls, there seems to be a confusion here. If you can repeat, you can read from the transcript itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I think perhaps asking the question again. If Mr. Bourgon asks his question again, it might be the cleanest way to...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I completely agree, Mr. President. I will even would do something better.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, were you working the next two days after the Orahovac events?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was loud and clear a moment ago. I asked them to give me some time off for rest. However, they were not able to give me these two or three days, instead they allowed me this exception to spend the nights at home; whereas, the obligation of all the other soldiers was to spend nights in the barracks. Since I wasn't able to be granted days off, they exceptionally allowed me to spend nights at home. This was the favour they did to me, to allow me to rest psychologically at home, at least overnight. Therefore, at that point, they were not able to give me a couple of days off because the situation in the field was extraordinary, and this is what I said a moment ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I'll move on to my next question. Yesterday, I referred to information that I have which comes from the chief of logistics. You mentioned a name yesterday. And according to what I mentioned to you or what comes from him, the Z Brigade command did not have juices in 1995. Now, this was at page 85 of the transcripts at lines 19 to 25, and my question to you this morning is very simple: Are you saying today that this information is wrong and that you saw juices or is it that you did not see what was in the boxes in your truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he answered this very clearly yesterday. He told you where the juices probably came from, and I think he was very poignant in his answer yesterday. I don't think we need to go through this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will move to my next but I feel it is important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, but he answered it yesterday. He has told you respective of what Sreten Milosevic may tell us. According to him, the position was as he said it yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, in the -- according to the same person, we have information that in the command kitchen, which was the only kitchen at the Zvornik Brigade command, they never made any doughnuts or pastries. My question is: Are you saying this information is incorrect or is it that you never saw what was put in your truck?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Objection to the form of the question. Because that information could be correct, and he could have seen what was put in his truck. That's a completely false choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think he can answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Go ahead, answer the question, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Shall I reply?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I will answer what I've already said, word by word. I confirm my previous statement word for word. Juices outside of the combat actions for the needs of the command and the officers and other clerks in the command were brought by me from Vitinka regularly. A contingent, a full van of crates of juices and mineral water, and this was left in the warehouse and used as needed. In the kitchen, sir, it's a modern kitchen, extremely well-equipped kitchen in which I had the privilege sometimes to eat better food and to socialise with the bakers, the officers, the heads of the kitchen, and I know well what can be made there. Secondly, many things were done in the state bakery, and they would be brought to the kitchen. They had the hygienic conditions to do that; and then from the kitchen and as for cookies and other sweet things, I said already that from private shops of -- then people -- the command paid for those Vitinka juices. I'm convinced I know that one part was paid for and one was donated, a part was donated by Vitinka, and I said that before.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I now move to my next topic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: It is necessary for this purpose, Mr. President, to go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, you asked for his statement to be brought in e-court. Do you have something to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No longer, Your Honour, because that was previously to the fact of that the "I had obtained some leave" and this changed my line of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps we can remove it now from the monitor, just in case it shows up during the broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You said, yesterday, I quote from page 45, lines 18 to 20, that you told the hospital staff and the doctor that you found the kid on a forest trail, somewhere around Srebrenica. And in your statement, which was from November 2005, you said that you found the kid on the road. My question is: Whichever is true, the road or the forest trail, you will agree with me that you did not tell the truth to the doctor and the hospital staff. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, you mentioned Srebrenica. Is that correct? Yes. Yes, you mentioned Srebrenica. I had the fortunate option of not going to Srebrenica. I went to all the fronts throughout Bosnia, but I did not go to Srebrenica. You mentioned Srebrenica. Please don't. That child, I said I didn't dare, because of the evil people, sir. I emphasise that. Because of my own protection, I said I found the child by the road. I was not on a forest trail. I was going along the asphalt and the asphalt road was close to the execution site. It was a normal road, not a forest trail. I don't know what you called it. I said, because I was afraid for a long time, and I didn't -- my brother knew, my sister-in-law knew, my close ones knew, and all the participants up there, participants in the event up there knew who took the child away. It's been entered, right, in the hospital, the information that it's a child from an execution site, from a place of execution, is not there. Even I picked up a man, one or two days later on the road, on the asphalt, not knowing who or what he was, assuming, and I stopped and I asked this wounded man. I asked him who he was, what he was. He said he was from Srebrenica, and he was asking me --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, we are getting completely away -- Mr. President, can we ask the Witness to please confine his answers to the questions that I ask, or else we will be here for a long time?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's partly true, but he has answered your question at the end of the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But, Mr. Witness, yesterday you said to Mr. Bourgon that you had told them, the hospital people or others, that you had come across the child on a forest trail, somewhere around Srebrenica. Was it a mistake on your part?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no. I never said anything like that in my life. I don't think that the Prosecution has that either. That is a mistake. It's impossible. I'm sorry that I am laughing, but -- but as I said, I had the fortune of not being issued with travel orders to have to take anyone, even the wounded. So I had no contact at all with Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So you must understand that the Defence counsel has to clarify that, because the transcript says so. Please proceed, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, my -- to finish with this topic concerning what you said to the hospital staff and the doctor, my question to you earlier on was that you did not tell them the truth of where you found the kid. Is that correct? Not looking for the reason why, I'm just asking why?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's answered that question. He's told you already. Yes, he didn't -- he wouldn't dare.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, please, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I said what I said. The reason why I said that I picked him up on the road and not at the execution site is for the welfare of the child, too. Because they would have reported, those evil people, that nurse, they would have told someone from the military structures that the child was brought from there, and they would have come to get him; and then he would have ended up the way it was meant, that he ends up, sir. I didn't -- I did it for the welfare of the child, afraid in the hospital. There is no institution in the world or a profession in the world without evil people, and for the sake of the child I said that. Everybody knows Milosevic. When Dragan knows, then anybody, if they knew, then everyone knew that I took the child where I took him.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let me move to my next topic. And in order to ask you my next question, I need you to confirm a few of the things that you said yesterday during your examination-in-chief. And yesterday at page 36, lines 15 to 20, you said that you took the kid from the truck where he had been placed by some soldier and you placed him in your van. I'm talking at the site. Is that what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sir. I wasn't interpreted well or perhaps I wasn't understood well. Let me repeat this word for word. They tried to place the child on the truck, but the child was convulsing, shrieking. The child may have been in a state of shock. I tried to prevent him from going into these convulsions. They were trying to place him on the truck; and as they were trying to put him on, I said, "Please let me take him in my van." I offered to take the child. Therefore, the child was never on the truck. I didn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The reason I ask this question is because the information you provided yesterday said that you took the child from the truck, and this is different from your statement. That is why I need to get your answer today. What I will now --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No, no. I'm sorry. I'm sorry, that's not what I said. I remember quite well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- move to my next question, if you will allow me. Can you confirm that after placing the Muslim boy, you drove into the direction of the Orahovac school at which time you were alone in the kid with the van [sic]? Is this your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I took the child on the orders, right, to leave him down there so that the next batch would finish him off. And on my own initiative, I decided to take him to the barracks in Karakaj. As I was approaching the barracks, I decided, and I did what I told you, and I took him to Zvornik. There was no one with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. That's all I wanted to know. Were you alone in the van with the kid, and is this your testimony and you have just confirmed this. I move to my next question. It was your testimony yesterday at page 37, lines 5 to 8, that you did not stop by the school in Orahovac and I quote, "Because I knew I could not leave him there." Is that correct, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I refer also to your testimony yesterday at page 37, lines 14 to 17, where in saying that you -- you testified about your decision is not to take him to the Zvornik Brigade first aid station because in your own words, "If I leave him there in the military facility, I need to explain to everyone how I came across this child." Is this your testimony also today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly. And for another reason. There they were not in a position to stitch him up. It was just a garrison clinic that could only provide some medical interventions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But yesterday you did not say that it was because they could not only -- they did not have the proper medical facilities. You said it was because I would need to explain it to everyone. Is that what you said yesterday?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Certainly, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I asked you this question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. And I was also afraid that the child would be taken back from there. I believe I stressed that as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, that's why I have my next point, because in your statement in 2005, at paragraph 23, you mention, "I was very afraid that although they might give him medical treatment in the beginning, he would then be taken for execution along with other prisoners." Do you confirm what you said in your statement today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I said many times, sir, many times over. They would have been taken away, because there were other prisoners there, as I said, extremists who were interrogated, whether -- the person who would kill a child would definitely pick him up from the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. At this stage I will share with you some information that I have, and then propose to you some -- or make some propositions to you in regards to your testimony. First, I would like to refer to information coming from Sreten Milosevic, which was provided to us by the Prosecution, and that is at the -- an interview which was conducted by the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, just for the record, form of the question, you've previously made rulings that the -- the person asking the questions should put the proposition to the witness, but it is not necessary and not proper to say that it came from another witness on the witness list. I think Your Honour said that yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't recall that the Trial Chamber said this. I recall my colleague making an objection to the fact that witnesses should not be compared one to the other. My case today is simply that I have information, which is provided to me by the Prosecution, and I need to put it to the witness to know which one is true: What the Prosecution gave us as information, or what the witness is saying today. It's my duty to put my case to the witness, and my colleague was complaining earlier on that he was not getting documents. Now we're talking about one of his own documents, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: That's completely not the issue, and I think Your Honours know it. He can put his case and he can put the information without --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can stop. Stop there, because we've got the witness in the courtroom in any case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. We don't really see much problem or legal problem in this issue. I mean strictly speaking the best way, the orthodox way to go about it would be to first put the proposition to the witness, see what he answers, and then you can actually again of course make reference to use or source of information, which sometimes can actually be asked for by -- by the Prosecution in any case. So let's proceed. I mean you know that we have adopted the orthodox system and the unorthodox system in these proceedings. So let's not make a storm in a teacup on this. Just put the proposition to the witness. You're free later on to tell him where you got it from.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, you mentioned that you drove the kid from the place where you picked him up alone in your van, straight to the hospital. I put it to you that this information is not true, that you stopped in the school in Orahovac, and that more people were in the van with you, that this van went to Zvornik command first, and then that you went to the hospital. And I further put it to you, Witness, that this person was the one to tell you who take the kid to the hospital and that it was not your decision. What do you say to that?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you this, sir, Your Honours: Before my departure for The Hague, or rather Holland, I had these sort of offers, so to speak, to say that they were with me and that things happened just the way you described them. And with the reason they offered me this possibility to lie, I didn't want to lie, they had reasons why they would say that. They were there, right, establishment-wise they had their assignments, duties, and those who gave them those assignments and duties knew why and how. I only know that of all those officers and those present, that all of them in 1996 at once, all those who were officers there were going to Tuzla and making great deals and businesses with Tuzla residents and Sarajevo residents. And everyone wondered in town how come they could be wandering around free when everyone knew what the positions they held. It's not true that anyone was with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, please let me -- let me make this easier. Do you deny stopping at the Orahovac school on that night with the kid? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You deny that you were not --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now, when I decided, once I decided not to leave him, of course I wouldn't stop.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you deny, Witness, that there were more people in the van driving with you and the kid that night? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said a moment ago that in the meantime some persons came up to me, approached me, and asked that I say that I was with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Witness, do you deny that the vehicle first stopped in the Zvornik command before you went to the hospital to drop off these people? Do you deny this information today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Defence counsel, for my truth and story, I am prepared to bear anything. To lie there where all the other liars lie for false testimony, every statement I make is truthful.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Witness, lastly, do you deny that it was Sreten Milosevic who told you to take the kid to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said a moment ago that there was no one with me, sir. How could he have told me that? He had to stay up there until everything was finished. Do you understand? I left. Everything stayed behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Let me share with you some information that I have, so to give you an opportunity to...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, Mr. McCloskey is present in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The information I would like to share with you is that Sreten Milosevic, now that is in the information he provided to the Prosecution, and he said that he was in the same vehicle as the kid who was injured, going to the Zvornik Brigade command. He also said -- told to the Prosecution that he remembers, just like you, that the kid was asking where his -- where was his daddy, and that he was crying. Sreten Milosevic also described for the Prosecution the injury to the leg suffered by the kid. And finally, according to Milosevic, the van first went to the brigade command and then to the hospital, and that it is him who told you to take the kid not to the first aid station, because it was poorly equipped and could not provide good care. Considering that this information -- now, I would ask you on the basis of this information that I just shared with you, is it your testimony today that this information is incorrect and that you stick -- do you stick to your story?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago I said that two more persons, who were tasked with being up there, offered me to tell them -- to tell that I was with them. I did not agree to that initiative. Sreten Milosevic was not with me, nor could he have been, naturally speaking, because he had duties up there and he was there all the time. And I left before everything was finished up there, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My next question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is not a chance for him being with me. Let me just tell you this: I would have wished or rather I wished that he had been with me, because he was a fine man, and there were some people who were really fine men and had to be up there. I am really sorry. I wish they could have been with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, did you ever tell the Prosecution or any other authority that you were invited to lie before the Tribunal today?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, I'm a lucky person. And with the Prosecutors who were there, there were many questions that were asked, whether they met with someone, with Milosevic and others who I knew and who I communicated --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I am sorry to interrupt you, Witness, but that is not my question.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- directly with.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I ask that the witness answer the question whether he was -- at any point did he ever tell the Prosecution or any other person in authority to he was invited by some people to provide false testimony before this Tribunal. The question is very simple, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Witness, could you please answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. No, never. Not the Prosecution, not any other BH structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I move to my next source on the same topic and for this I need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's do that. Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, according to the person I just mentioned to you in closed session, he also says he was in the van with you that night. He identified you as being the driver and being there with the kid and three other persons, including Sreten Milosevic. This witness further stated --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Mr. President, I'll just give the reference of this. This is the testimony of (redacted) (redacted).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, this witness or this person -- sorry, further stated that he was picked up by you further along the road and not at the school, because he had started to walk back towards the command. And he also confirmed that the van went first to the Zvornik Brigade command where he and the other passengers stayed and you continued on to the hospital with the kid. On the basis of this information, I invite you once again to say whether you stick to your story and whether you say this person provided false testimony under oath. Which one is it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't think it should be phrased like that. Just ask him whether he sticks to his store. Asking him whether the other one whether the other one committed perjury is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: If I may say, Your Honour, I'm sorry to interrupt, but that is exactly the reason why I make these types of objections. I am not trying to slow things down, but that is what -- in old English text, that is what is called that the mischief of that type of question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Just answer the following question: Having been given this information, do you still stick to your story that at no time did you have anyone in your van with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, (redacted)

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Can we go into private, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And you messed it up now, because we have to redact at least four times now. So let's go back to private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I will say my question once again. I have information coming from another person who was in the vehicle that night who says he was in the vehicle that night, and he identified you as the driver and he also remembered detail that you provided some chocolate to the Muslim boy on your way to the Z Brigade command. On the basis of this information, straightforward, do you stick with your story, and were you still alone in the van that night?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I didn't offer anything to the child. It never crossed my mind. I was in a hurry to -- to get there as soon as possible before he bled to death, you know. There were two wounds to be stitched up. There was no time to tary. I was in a hurry and I didn't give any cakes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I think it is time for a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it has to be a 30-minute break because we had redactions towards the end of the sitting. So we will reconvene in 30 minutes' time.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours. I just wonder if we can -- if there is an estimate just for our planning purposes of how long this is going to go on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you can discuss it amongst yourselves during the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I promised that I would give you an answer about the motion for safe conduct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, let's go into private session, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, we will continue later on with respect to the place where you said that you picked up the Muslim boy that night, and I have more information that I will share with you from people who were actually there that night. But for now, I'd like to address a different topic, and that is the time that you arrived for the first time at the Orahovac school. Correct me if I'm wrong, but you are quite familiar with the surroundings of the Orahovac school, is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps it would be too much to say that I know the surroundings, but I know in detail the area around the road. But as for the environs, I don't know what you mean. You mean the part behind the "sava" [as interpreted], I don't know. What I could see around me, around the road, that I know to an inch, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And could you see houses in front of the school, and do you happen to know to whom these houses belong to?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are houses, I think belonging to the Vidovics; Before them are the houses of the Matics; the house that is near the road itself, it's a small house. I don't know whose it was, the owners changed; I don't know anybody's house behind the gym. I don't know anybody's house. There were some shops there, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I needed this information because I will be providing you later on with a plan of the area which has some names on it, and I wanted to be -- after showing this plan to my colleague, there are some names on it. So before I would give it to you, I needed to know what information you knew about the surroundings.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: If I may recall the exhibit that was used yesterday by the Prosecution, 1691, the way it was marked by the witness yesterday.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction on page 39, line 4, the word should be "gym" and not the "sava."

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Is it possible to have the one...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, it's there now. We have it now.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I ask you to look at this picture, which -- on which you made two markings yesterday. And we are in open session, but this is not being broadcasted. And it says 101 anyway, so I think we can proceed with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: There is no problem. I see no problem, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I would like you to confirm, Witness, by looking at this picture, that the first mark that you did, and I would like you to circle around where the truck was in which the prisoners were loaded.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I understand that the markings you just made with the same colour, I should have asked for a different colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, because this will change the exhibit from yesterday, unless we can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It won't. This will be a new exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The markings you just made now, this is the truck in which the prisoners were loaded. Is that the case?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The -- this part next to the gym, that's the back part of the bus, so the truck -- the back part of the truck. So the truck was turned towards Krizevci.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And this is where --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment. For the record, the marking that the witness has made in sort of an unfinished rectangle is approximate, or around the previous mark X that he had made yesterday. Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, the -- the truck which was -- in which the prisoners were loaded, this is the truck in which you said yesterday that they put some kind of ladder or steps for the prisoners to go up on that truck. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And yesterday in your testimony, you mentioned that a corridor was made out to lead the prisoners from the school into that -- into the truck. I'd like you to draw the corridor that you're talking about, the way it was made, to the best of your ability.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, the second mark that was there yesterday, this is where I understand that your van was. Can you circle the second mark to show where your van was?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Did you see, Witness, any other vehicles around the school at that time?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was a military or an army jeep there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And could you locate and put where that military jeep was, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If I may interrupt you for the time being, so that we try to give it more clarity. Witness, let's start with the first marking that you made, indicating the location of the truck. Can I ask you to write -- put down the letter T? T for tango.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Next to the truck, next to the truck.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, next to the marking that you made indicating the location of the corridor, could I ask you please to put or to mark the letter C?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, next to the marking indicating the location of your van, could you please put the letter V?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And next to the other marking which indicates the location of the military jeep, could you put the letter J?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. May I clarify with the court officer that where the vehicle with the J is drawn, that this will be picked up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes. I've just verified it myself. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, Witness, I will ask you to look at this picture once again, and I look at on the side, on the right side at the bottom we see something that could be a vehicle. I'm just asking you if the jeep you are talking about was further away from this place or was it around that area?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see clearly the end of the road; the edge of the road, and looking down from the left on the right side of the road was where the jeep was, more or less, approximately the way I indicated it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, the last thing I'd like you to indicate on this -- on this sketch is yesterday you spoke about one of the prisoners who tried to escape, and who was followed by some people who ran after him. I'd like you to indicate, if we can use another colour, is that possible? And indicate where you saw this prisoner escape and which way did the prisoner escape?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Halfway into the yard from the gate to the entrance into the hall, halfway on the road. I didn't see that, but it's probably where he ripped off his blindfold, and then he ran behind the building here, and from what I could see they shot at him. I don't know if he was hit in the course of that. But behind the building when you couldn't see him, you could hear bursts of fire; and then after that, those two young men with the rifles returned by themselves, returned alone.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness -- let me handle this, Mr. Bourgon. Okay. Thank you for that information which you also gave us yesterday. Now, we need to -- we would like you to put -- mark the letter P on the location where you first saw this prisoner on the point of escaping, before he started to escape. Where was he? Put the letter P, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So for the record, the witness has put the letter P in blue, and then traced the route that this prisoner would have taken in his attempt to escape. Is that correct? Okay. Thank you. I see the witness nodding. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I will now, on the basis of this sketch -- well first, were there any other vehicles that you can remember being there at the school on that day?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: From what I can remember, there were no other cars at that moment. No other vehicles. I stayed there for ten or 15 minutes, sir, until the truck came from the direction of Krizevici, a new group entered. That was the time I stayed there. And during that time, I didn't see a large number of vehicles there. Perhaps I missed one, but there were no military vehicles there anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, my next question, Witness -- did you wish to add something?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were in the yards of the other houses, perhaps they had taken their vehicles to the yards of the houses because of the road. The road was being normally used. The villagers from the surrounding area were using the road. The traffic was not suspended or banned on the road.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, yesterday you mentioned that (redacted)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You are right. You are right. We did. So let's redact this, and go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, on the basis of information provided by witnesses in this case who mentioned that the corridor that you are talking about, there was such a corridor created, but that was when the prisoners arrived with the buses and were placed initially in the gym. I suggest to you that you did not see the prisoners being loaded in that truck, or that you were present earlier when those buses arrived.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's take them one by one, because I think they're two different things. Put your first question, Mr. Bourgon, again; which is a repetition of the previous question.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will say my question again in two parts, and I heard there was a mistake in the translation. My first proposition to you is that -- or even I will make it easier. The fact that the corridor was made out to escort the prisoners is a story that you heard and that you never saw.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Everything I said is the truth. I didn't see a single corridor,, I didn't see a single bus bringing the people there. I was some 15 minutes there, and then some 15 minutes until the whole thing was finished. I didn't see a single corridor. If it's the corridor you've been asking me about, as well as His Honour, I was referring to two or three soldiers standing on one side and two to three soldiers standing on the other side. They stood in a relaxed manner, carrying weapons. It wasn't a corridor. I'm not sure how many people you're envisaging to have been there. You see, the prisoners were quite relaxed. They were told that they were going to be an exchange, for a prisoner exchange. When they were entering or rather climbing on the truck, everybody was telling them, "Do not fear, you're going for an exchange." They were treated correctly. Well, if you can say correctly. They were brought some water into the gym. I brought two sacks of bread. My later impression was that these soldiers, who were there, were not aware of what was actually happening. That was the impression I got.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. One last question on this sketch. You mentioned in your testimony yesterday that you yourself followed the truck as long -- along with the jeep. You were the third vehicle in that convoy. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And I propose to you today that you cannot tell or identify who was in that convoy from the army of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: How should I know, since I didn't have even five or six minutes of dealings with the army throughout the war. I used to drive shifts of soldiers for a while, and I could tell by the looks which one of them were aggressive or evil. I didn't care about knowing what their names were or maintaining any sort of contact. And I know full well the order in which we were in this line, and I know that soldiers were standing at the ready with their weapons on the jeep to intervene, should some of the prisoners try to escape from the truck; although, I didn't see anything but the one incident I told you next to the gym, and then I know of some other incidents unrelated to this event.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Now, I'd like to -- yesterday you provided some information concerning --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: We can -- I'm finished with this exhibit, so maybe we can just put the date, today's date to show that.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Can you, Witness, put the date. Just where you put 101, simply put today's date, and that is the 23rd of February.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So we'll save it, Madam Registrar, and give it a number. Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I now move on to my next question, which deals with your description of Drago Nikolic was doing in Orahovac. And I put it to you that this was information that you did not know or remember when you met with the Prosecution, both in November of 2005 as well as in April of 2006, because that is not mentioned in either document. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you referring to the text with the -- in communicating with

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Stop, stop. I'm sorry I have to stop you because then we will have to redact an entire page or so. In the meantime, Madam Registrar, you need to redact where necessary, from lines 17 of the previous page until now. Let's go into private session to deal with this, because he keeps on mentioning these names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And the question -- yes, you can repeat it.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The question is, Witness: I'm simply saying that in your first statement the actions of Drago Nikolic are not described. In your information we have from April 2006, the actions of Drago Nikolic are not described; and then suddenly in December of 2006, for the first time you speak about Drago Nikolic. I'd like to know why this is so.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: A moment ago you confused me. I thought you -- you asked me about

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Never-ending story. Redact that and let's proceed. Thank you. We are talking of Drago Nikolic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Would you like me to repeat the question, or...

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, no. It's quite clear now. No problem. Mr. Interpreter [as interpreted], I know that the person you're asking about, that he was in charge of prisoner exchanges at the barracks of captured soldiers, Serbs and Muslims, and this was the story I heard from the people at the barracks that he was a very good at what he was doing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, one moment. Stop, stop. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just want to make something clear --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I want to make something clear to in fairness in reference to the question. The question was: "And then suddenly in December 2006, for the first time you speak about Drago Nikolic," and I don't think that is what my friend's assertion would be. I don't think he is asserting that would he didn't speak about Drago Nikolic in his very first statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you have to say about that, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Indeed, if at that time I did not say "actions of," my proposition to the witness is that he never described any actions of Drago Nikolic in November 2005, in April 2006, and that it is only in December that suddenly we have information provided by him by -- about the actions of Drago Nikolic. I'd like to know why this is so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you understand the question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Please proceed to answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a moment ago what was Drago who I knew like. You could never tell what the person was doing. You could always see him going around alone; and then later on, sitting in cafes, I would hear stories of Drago as being such and such a person, and then stories by various people. It was in this way that I learnt later on, because for many of these people I didn't know what their functions were. I saw him there on the spot where I did, and later on I heard that he was in charge of security. Truth to tell, I thought that he was a Chief of Police; I mean military police. I found out later that --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So the information you possessed about Drago Nikolic you found out about after the events and, actually, you didn't know what was his duty in July of 1995. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995, yes, I knew then. Throughout the war, I didn't know what his duty was. I knew about that first one related to the exchanges. But I didn't know that a person holding the position of a security officer would be dealing with these matters, would be dealing with exchanges. I didn't know which function or role such a person would hold. It was later on that I found out that he was in charge of security. I knew other security officers, I cooperated with them, I did many things with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I need to interrupt you because I need you to get to the question that I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And I think, if you phrase it the way I'm going to suggest to you, and I hope you will appreciate this, it will probably help. May I suggest to you that you put to the witness first what according to you in December 2006 were the actions that he describes in relation to Drago Nikolic. That's number one. Then ask him why, on previous occasions, he had never given such a description.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Mr. President, he described yesterday actions of Drago Nikolic, so that's not what I -- my interest is why is it that this information only came out in December of 2006 and not before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Witness, I think it's clear now. What is required from you is an explanation why these actions that Mr. Bourgon is referring to, you only mentioned in December 2006 and not before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think until this moment the witness had understood your question. Could you kindly put Mr. Nikolic's conduct as he described yesterday and then ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Yesterday, Witness, you said that you saw Drago Nikolic at the Orahovac school. I will quote what you said yesterday. Now, I look at the transcript. I do not have the -- the exact reference with me now, I'm looking for it. What I'm simply putting to you is yesterday you said that he was at the school and that he was to quote, "listening and issuing orders which were not really orders," and that there was really no need for orders. I'm paraphrasing because I don't have the exact reference. Why is this information you did not provide before December of 2006?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: You see, I'm neither a lawyer nor an intern to be able to know the time-line and to know which are the most important things to tell you. Perhaps I should have told this at the time, but we didn't go into details and this may have been the reason. I'm not -- many lawyers are not really skillful at some issues and some situations.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I will stop with this topic and move on to the next topic, which is the final thing I want to address today and that is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, can I help you, the exact page is 7573, and it's starting from line 4. So can I read it for you?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: No need, Judge. I will move on, because I cannot get across to the fact why the information came later but that's perfectly fine with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The last area I want to cover, Witness, is concerning the time you spent where you say that you picked up the kid. Now, first, I will ask you some questions as to what you say that you saw there. My first question is -- are we in private session, because we don't need to be in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are on open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My first question is: Did you see any heavy machinery where you say that you picked up the kid?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. Not a single machine, not a -- not even the smallest of loaders, none of those construction machines or tractors.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And, Witness, did you see any other vehicles at that place?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some cars there. I can't remember well. There were cars on their way up to the village that would stop and look; and even down at Orahovac, you have people standing behind their fence and watching out of their yards and observing what was going on. You see, in such a situation, I could not be relaxed enough to be able to take in all of what was going on, what people were saying or doing. It was very difficult, very difficult. I was focused on the events, on the atrocities.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. My question to you is that -- my proposition to you on the basis that information that I have is that you are not the one who picked up the Muslim boy and took that -- took him from the execution site that day. Do you stick to your story or do you want me to share with you that information?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, at the time Yugoslavia was in communism, I was the only one having a roast on a spit for Christmas --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I am sorry. My question is very, very precise.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- and celebrating St. George.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Do you maintain your story even in the face of the proposition that you were not the one who took the kid from the site? Do you maintain your testimony?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: God knows and people know and those in the hospital know who brought him in. All those who tell a different story, well, they will be given by God what they deserve.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, my question --

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I lie, you can kill me.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, my question does not relate to who took the kid to the hospital. My question relates to who took the kid from where you say you picked him up, and I'm saying that you are not the person who picked up the kid that night.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What I --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, sir. I've been carrying this around my neck for 30 years. This is my faith. Jesus Christ and Virgin Mary on the other side. I am not a false -- novice in faith. I have been a believer for years and years, and I swear on this that I took this child into the van, just as I stated in all my statements. I have been living all my life with this truth and with these horrors, and I would not wish something like this to befall you and to be convincing persons who are telling the truth, that they are, in fact, not telling the truth. I don't know why you're doing this, for money, but I'm telling you that I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I will share with you some information that I have from a potential witness, but before that I need to go into closed session for one question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a short while.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are back in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, I have obtained information from a potential Defence witness, according to whom the Muslim child was placed on the back of the military truck which drove away with the kid in the back, and this person says that having seen with his own eyes the kid being in the back of a truck driving back to the school in Orahovac. On the basis of this information, I suggest that you did not tell the truth when you said that you put the kid in your van and that you left the site with him.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I stand by what I said word for word. Let me not repeat this again.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the way it was on the first day and will be all my life.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, before I move to my next question, I request that the witness be given the warning at Rule 91(1) [sic].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: When that kind of proposition is put to the witness from a potential Defence witness, I think we're entitled to know who it is on our side when this is being read out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Our position is --

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: May I make one other -- sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: With this specific question, you were seen doing -- this was seen by somebody with their own eyes. In that case, it may be appropriate to tell the witness who this is, to help him answer. I mean he has answered that he is sticking by his story. But when he says this person saw you, then the witness can possibly say whether or not that person was even around.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, are you prepared to tell the witness who this person is?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: For the same reason as why the Prosecution has been asking for all these protective measures, this particular person, and the next one I'm going to speak about, is not willing at this time to have their names disclosed nor to have any information, because they are afraid for their security. These are two persons that would -- that have -- that provided information to the Defence that they were present on that location; and both of these persons, there will be filings and motions put forward to the Trial Chamber with ex parte information.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll delay our decision on the issue that you raise until later. More or less we are there, but it requires a little bit more discussion amongst ourselves, although we'll be in a position to come to a quick conclusion later on. Let's proceed with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to make a correction to the transcript, further to what my colleague said a few moments ago. Because I quote my colleague at page 59, line 25, and page 60, lines 1 to 4. My colleague said, in this case, it may be appropriate to tell the witness who this is too, when he says this person saw you. Now, I refer back to what you said in the transcript --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He didn't say that..

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- on page 59, lines 4 to 10. I did not say that that person had seen the witness; on the contrary, this person did not see the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And that is what why my proposition, as I'm telling to the witness, that he is not telling the truth when he says that he was the one to pick up the kid.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Sir, do you maintain your testimony?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Sorry. I believe he answered that before we got into all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I am not a lawyer, so I'm going to ask you to intervene, if necessary, or I don't know what. But the counsel asserted that (redacted) went to the barracks with me and that I stopped off at barracks, and now, again, there are some claims by witnesses -- that he has witnesses that a truck picked up the child and took him away. What is true of all of that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's answer the proposition once and for all, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, he did answer, my colleague is correct. I looked at the transcript and he said that he stands by his --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: -- Word for word, too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: My request, Mr. President, before I move to my last question, had to deal with the warning at Rule 91(A), which reads that the Chamber may proprio motu or at the request of a party may warn a witness of the duty to tell the truth and the consequences that may result from a failure to do so. I would request, Mr. President, that the witness be given this warning at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: I just ask what the basis is before the question has even been asked for him to go ahead with this. It seems like it's just a -- a way to try to rattle the witness to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I don't think I need a basis for placing that request, according to Rule 91 Alpha, but I have a full basis because for the duration of my cross-examination the witness has been denying constantly propositions based on information that I possess. Before I move to my last question, he should be given this warning. He should be given the opportunity. It is my duty to put my case to him. It is my duty that he has the opportunity to know what the consequences will be in the sense of what the information he is providing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Well, I think the witness was put on notice at the beginning of his testimony that his responsibility is to speak the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: As I said earlier on, I think we put the witness on notice at the beginning of his testimony that he is under an obligation to testify the truth, pursuant to the solemn declaration he made, and we don't believe there is any need for us to resort to Rule 91(A) at this stage, Mr. Bourgon. He knows what his responsibilities are.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I will move to another question, for which I need to go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We are in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Witness, yesterday, we discussed the two interviews that took place between you and the Prosecution, the first one taking place in November 2005 and the second one taking place on 10th of April, 2006. I would like you to confirm what you said yesterday concerning your relationship with the Prosecution, and I quote you from page 65 of the transcript yesterday, lines 3 to 5. "This is no secret. That is what was read out to me because I announced to the Prosecutors that I would be giving no statements unless I am granted this and that, such and such a thing." Can you confirm that this was your motivation for providing testimony before this Court today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He can answer the question, and -- but what I object to is the form of the question which misstates and mischaracterises the record. There -- the witness testified about how he wanted protective measures and that he was concerned for his family. He never said that his motive for giving statements was for any particular purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he's being asked now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: He's asking him to confirm that that's what he said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's what he's being asked now.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can reply, no problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead. Please give us your answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, I have just heard from the Prosecutor this debate; the motive for the request for protective measures. Well, I'm not some pauper, a poor person asking for protection and a chance in life. I have done a lot of things in life, and perhaps you don't know about that. Even before the war I had a lot, and everybody was asking where did he get this that. Even during the war I made a lot and I had an expensive car, and everybody was asking me what was it. After the war again I made a lot, and I had a house and I had a lot of other things. And always people would ask themselves, how does he do it? Even now I am well off. I am not motivated by any reasons. All that I want I've achieved much more than many others. I have achieved a lot, believe me, as a worker, as a driver, at an international level. I have a lot, and I am rich as a man.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Bourgon. I understand that some Defence counsel wish, and others don't wish to cross-examine the witness. Can you enlighten us on this? I understand Mr. Haynes you are require about 20 minutes or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you wish us to have the break now and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It would be seem to be sensible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Do you think we can live with 25 minutes? Okay. We'll have a 25-minute break instead of a 30-minute one. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Witness.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I represent Vinko Pandurevic, who, in 1995, was the commander of the Zvornik Brigade. I dare say you remember that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS PW-101 [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And I have just a few questions for you, but I'm going to ask you to do me two favours, if you would.
